newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says it killed 43 Kurd guerrillas in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says it killed 43 Kurd guerrillas in Iraq.

text.p: Turkish air force planes carried out three separate air raids into neighbouring northern Iraq last month in which 43 Kurdish guerrillas were killed, the state-run Anatolian news agency said on Wednesday.

It said F-4 and F-16 planes from air bases in the towns of Malatya and Diyarbakir bombed two Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebel camps in northern Iraq. It did not give specific dates for the operations.
Anatolian quoted officials in southeastern Turkey as saying air strikes would continue if guerrilla bases were spotted during reconnaissance flights in the mountainous border region.
The PKK uses camps in northern Iraq as a part of its 12-year-old fight for self-rule in southeastern Turkey. More than 21,000 people have been killed in the conflict.
Baghdad has often complained to the United Nations about Turkish border incursions in northern Iraq, where Iraqi Kurds encouraged by the West have held control since shortly after the 1991 Gulf War.
